faqs.q: What causes a sprain or a strain?
faqs.a: A sprain often involves an injury that moves a joint too far in either direction, such as falling and landing on your hand, which can cause a wrist sprain. Also, a blow to the body that causes the ankle to twist and turn can lead to an ankle sprain. For strains, the most common cause is overuse, which leads to a chronic strain. An acute strain happens suddenly, and it is most often caused by a blow to the body or overstretching, which is common in weightlifting, sprinting and sport activities.

faqs.q: I want to recover from my sprain or strain as quickly as possible so I can return to playing my sport. How do I speed up the recovery process?
faqs.a: The best way to speed up the recovery process after a sprain or strain is to implement the R.I.C.E. method, which involves resting, icing, compressing and elevating the affected area. Additionally, it is important to seek medical assistance as soon after the injury as possible for proper diagnosis in treatment, especially when attempting to make a fast recovery. Most importantly, resist the urge to return to what caused the injury (e.g., sports, running, etc.) until a full recovery is made.

faqs.q: I have been trying to stay active despite my sprain or strain, and it has not gotten any better. Is there any way I can stay active with a sprain or a strain?
faqs.a: The short answer is no. The only way to truly recover from a sprain or a strain is to rest and properly apply the treatment necessary. It is important to be patient with a sprain or strain, as there is a high chance of re-injury if it is not properly rested. With that said, you may be able to alter the way you practice, especially while playing sports. If you endure an ankle sprain while playing basketball, perhaps find an area of practice that does not involve any use of the affected area, such as shooting baskets in a chair.

faqs.q: How long does it take to fully recover from a sprain or a strain?
faqs.a: The time it takes to make a full recovery from a sprain or strain depends on the severity of the injury. If you suffer from a grade I sprain, it typically heals within one to two weeks after the injury, assuming proper rest and treatment is administered. For grade II sprains and strains, it often takes four to six weeks to make a full recovery. For grade III strains, which typically involve a tear, it can take more than 12 weeks to make a full recovery. Keep in mind that every injury is different, and the exact recovery time depends on various factors that are hard to predict.

faqs.q: Is there anything I can do to prevent a sprain or strain from occurring?
faqs.a: There are several steps you can take to prevent a sprain or strain from occurring, although the risk is always there during physical activity. To give yourself the best chance possible to prevent a sprain or strain, be sure to conduct a warm-up activity, and then go through a thorough stretching routine. There are also braces (for joints) or compression sleeves (for muscles) for particular areas to provide more stability and safety of that area. Keep in mind, it is important to warm up the body before stretching.

definitions.def: Pain directly related to soft tissue damage. Typically lasts three to six months or less. Resolves itself gradually as the injured tissues heal.

Chronic pain is pain that lasts for longer than three months. May gradually become worse and recur periodically, even after the tissues have healed and for no apparent reason. Commonly associated with lower back pain, headache, and arthritic pain.

There are three different degrees (or grades) of sprain and strains. A grade I strain or sprain often is not serious and suggests the ligament, muscle or tendon is only partially stretched, whereas a grade III strain may lead to a tear.

A band of tough connective tissue that holds two bones or pieces of cartilage together in a join. When a ligament is overstretched or torn, it leads to a sprain, which can be painful and require treatment.
The organ system of our body that muscles, ligaments and tendons belong to. The musculoskeletal system provides support and stability while our body moves.
Pushing the body physically beyond its limits, often resulting in a strain, sprain, or more serious injury.
A highly recommended course of treatment for many sprains and strains. The R.I.C.E. method stands for rest, ice, compression and elevation.

A stretching or tearing of a ligament, which is the fibrous tissue in our bodies that connects our bones and our joints. A sprain can happen anywhere there is a ligament, but it most commonly occurs to an ankle, wrist or knee.
A force or pressure exerted on a part of the body to an extreme or dangerous degree; a strained muscle is the product of strenuous activity or accidental tear from pulling or stretching.
Flexible fibrous collagen tissue that connects a muscle to a bone. Although a tendon is flexible, it typically is not elastic and can overstretch or tear during intense exercise.

h1: Strep Throat Treatment Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
The early symptoms of strep throat can often feel like the onset of a cold or flu. It is characterized primarily by a sore, scratchy throat and is often associated with fever or headache. Though rest and store-bought medicine can sometimes be enough to treat certain respiratory illnesses, strep throat is best treated with professional care.

Strep throat treatment is available at call Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area. This condition is highly contagious and may lead to serious complications if left untreated. Visit us today or call (949) 204-1334 to schedule an appointment or to learn more about our services.

Understanding Strep Throat

Strep throat is a bacterial infection that makes the throat feel sore and scratchy. It only accounts for a small portion of sore throats. However, it is crucial to diagnose since, if left untreated, severe complications may arise. These include kidney inflammation and rheumatic fever, which, in turn, can lead to inflamed joints or heart valve damage. Strep throat can affect people of all ages.

Since strep throat is a bacterial infection, it requires antibiotic treatment. Though home remedies may alleviate some of its symptoms, only professional treatment can ensure that it does not spread or worsen. As such, individuals should seek medical attention as soon as they suspect they may have strep throat.

Strep throat is a bacterial infection that makes the throat feel sore and scratchy.

Causes of Strep Throat

Strep throat is caused by group A Streptococcus bacteria or Streptococcus pyogenes. This group of bacteria is also known as group A strep, or GAS. It is a highly contagious bacterial infection that usually spreads through respiratory droplets, such as sneezes or coughs.

Individuals can become infected with strep throat if they touch their eyes, mouth, or nose after being exposed to group A strep. Alternatively, they can become infected after sharing food or drink with an infected person or coming into contact with a contaminated object, then touching the face.

Strep throat is caused by group A Streptococcus bacteria or Streptococcus pyogenes.

Symptoms of Strep Throat

Some people may experience more severe strep throat symptoms than others. The most common signs of strep throat include:

  • Chills
  • Headache
  • Loss of appetite
  • Sore, red throat with white patches
  • Sudden fever, especially one that is 101 degrees Fahrenheit or higher
  • Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
  • Trouble swallowing

Those with mild cases of strep throat may not experience much more than a sore throat. For this reason, they may confuse strep throat with the common cold, a sinus infection, postnasal drip, or acid reflux. In any case, strep throat symptoms generally develop within five days of exposure to the strep bacteria.

…strep throat symptoms generally develop within five days of exposure to the strep bacteria.

Treating Strep Throat

Our primary care doctor can determine the severity of a patient's strep throat and treat it accordingly. Since strep throat is a bacterial infection, this will almost always involve a prescribed antibiotic treatment to stop the spread. Patients may stop taking their medication once they see their symptoms improve. However, this does not mean that the infection has been killed off entirely. As such, patients must complete the entire course of medication to minimize the risk of relapse.

There are various antibiotics for strep throat treatment. Penicillin and amoxicillin are the most common. If patients are allergic, they may be prescribed azithromycin or another course of antibiotics instead. For some patients, multiple antibiotic treatments may be necessary.

Since strep throat is a bacterial infection, [treatment] will almost always involve a prescribed antibiotic treatment to stop the spread.

Diagnosing Strep Throat

It can be challenging to differentiate between strep throat and other illnesses. Only a medical professional can make a correct diagnosis. As such, individuals should seek medical attention if they are experiencing any of the following symptoms:

  • Dark, red blotches or spots on the tonsils or top of the mouth
  • Difficulty breathing
  • Difficulty swallowing
  • Sore throat lasting longer than two days
  • Sore throat with a pink, fine, sandpaper-like rash on the skin
  • Sore throat with white patches

A primary care doctor can examine the throat for any signs of inflammation. They may also ask the patient about any other symptoms and check their neck for swollen lymph nodes. If there is reason to believe that the patient may have strep, the physician may conduct a rapid strep test in the office. This test involves swabbing the back of the throat with a long cotton swab to collect a sample and then sending it to a lab to look for any signs of bacteria. Results should be available in around five minutes. If the test comes back negative, but the physician still has concerns, further testing may be necessary.

It can be challenging to differentiate between strep throat and other illnesses. Only a medical professional can make a correct diagnosis.

faqs.q: Can I be vaccinated against group A strep?
faqs.a: No. As of yet, there are no vaccines available against group A Streptococcus bacteria. Fortunately, there are still many preventative measures you can take. Remember to cover your mouth and nose when sneezing or coughing, and wash your hands frequently. Avoid sharing personal items with others, especially those that may be infected.

faqs.q: Do tonsils serve a purpose?
faqs.a: Yes. Tonsils are the red, oval clumps of tissue at the back and sides of the throat. They facilitate the tonsils in intercepting any germs that enter the body through the nose and throat. Tonsils have infection-fighting cells and antibodies to limit the spread of germs. It is not uncommon for tonsils to become inflamed in cases of strep throat.

faqs.q: Can strep throat clear up on its own?
faqs.a: Yes. The body may get rid of strep throat within two to five days. However, this is typically only true for minor cases. For more severe cases, proper treatment is necessary to prevent any potential complications.

faqs.q: Can I still go to school or work if I have strep throat?
faqs.a: No. Strep throat is highly contagious, and you may easily pass it onto someone else. Stay home until your fever has passed and you have taken antibiotics for at least 24 hours.

faqs.q: When should I go to the emergency room for strep throat?
faqs.a: Strep throat is usually not an emergency. Still, some cases require immediate attention. If you are experiencing drooling and significant difficulty breathing or swallowing, you should visit a hospital as soon as possible. Otherwise, we can help treat you.

description: Telemedicine offers patients remote healthcare during after-hours and allows for more expanded access.
h1: Telemedicine Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
Telemedicine has broadened the spectrum for patients needing care. Advancements in medical technologies have expanded access to allow more people to attain essential health care when they need it. Telemedicine includes various services, ranging from advice to immediate prescription filling without the need for in-person visits.

At Orange County House Calls, we offer telemedicine services for patients who are unable to come into the clinic for any reason. Our team can assess your condition from the comfort of your home and discuss the next steps, whether it be coming in for an examination or taking certain measures to relieve your symptoms. To learn more about our services or schedule an appointment, call (949) 204-1334 today.

Understanding Telemedicine

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), telemedicine is "the use of electronic and telecommunication technologies" that allow patients access to health care without visiting a physical office. Through various forms of technology, including phone, tablet, or computer, patients can seek medical advice for non-emergency conditions and discuss symptoms with their practitioner. These appointments often involve photos, video, or camera engagement, which provides the doctor with a visual of the condition when appropriate.

Telemedicine appointments are most commonly used when a patient is unable to physically come into the office, during after-hours, and for monitoring an ongoing condition. The three types of telemedicine include:

  • Interactive Medicine: when physicians and patients communicate in real-time
  • Remote Patient Monitoring: allows practitioners to monitor data on blood pressure, blood sugar levels, etc
  • Store-and-Forward: collecting and sharing patients’ health information with other healthcare professionals or specialists
Through various forms of technology, including phone, tablet, or computer, patients can seek medical advice for non-emergency conditions and discuss symptoms with their practitioner.

How Telemedicine Works

Patients will have access to an online portal with personal login information. The portal allows patients to make an appointment, list their symptoms and concerns, and ask any pertinent questions. The physician will then assess the case and determine whether they could offer their advice through a reply or the patient would benefit from an in-person visit or online appointment.

Once an appointment is scheduled, the patient and practitioner meet over the online portal. We may request that the patient use video or send photos for cases in which we would need to visually assess the condition. During the appointment, we will discuss the patient's symptoms, record important medical information, update any changes to their health, make recommendations for their current case, and send any necessary lab work or prescriptions.

Patients will have access to an online portal with personal login information.

Types of Telemedicine Services

Patients often seek telemedicine services for non-emergency cases to acquire medical advice on a certain condition. They may also communicate changes in an ongoing condition that the physician is already aware of. Lastly, many telemedicine appointments are made after-hours or by patients outside of the network interested in receiving care from a particular practitioner.

In any case, telemedicine services may include situations such as:

  • Diagnoses of common medical problems such as headache, sore throat, back pain, and digestive troubles
  • Faster refill of short-term medical prescriptions
  • Holidays, weekends, late-night, or any other situation when regular medical care is not possible
  • Inquiries about various medical issues for home treatments
  • Patient inability to leave the house due to sickness or bad weather conditions
  • Post-treatment check-ins or follow up for chronic care
Patients often seek telemedicine services for non-emergency cases to acquire medical advice on a certain condition.

Benefits of Telemedicine

Telemedicine benefits both patients and practitioners. It allows patients to:

  • Access their health record and monitorization remotely
  • Save on travel time/transportation costs
  • Send and receive messages from their doctor using chat messaging or email
  • Talk to their doctor live over the phone or video chat without leaving the comfort of their home or office
  • Take fewer days off of school/work

It benefits practitioners by:

  • Attaining a larger clientele
  • Expanding access to patients in and out of network
  • Having access to patients’ data and sharing information easily with other practitioners
  • Reducing number of visits to clinic
  • Reducing wait time for services

Although telemedicine has been around for many years, it has expanded substantially after the pandemic. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, many people requiring care turned to telehealth services and realized their benefits even after the order was lifted. Today, many patients use telemedicine for many aspects of their healthcare, including primary care, dental care, mental health care, and specialty care.

Today, many patients use telemedicine for many aspects of their healthcare, including primary care, dental care, mental health care, and specialty care.

Telemedicine consultations and treatments are available at our office. The Orange County House Calls team looks forward to meeting you and helping you through your symptoms. Call our office at 949-204-1334 to learn more about telemedicine, any of our services, or to schedule an appointment.

faqs.q: Who uses telemedicine?
faqs.a: Healthcare providers offer telemedicine and telecommunication services to provide various forms of medical care, including dentists, primary care physicians, mental health specialists, and other medical specialists. It is important to ask or look online to ensure your healthcare provider offers the service before making an appointment.

faqs.q: What is the difference between telemedicine and telehealth?
faqs.a: The biggest difference between telemedicine and telehealth is the type of care provided. Telemedicine typically involves clinical care services while telehealth can include both clinical and non-clinical services. These services are both offered remotely.

faqs.q: What technologies do I need to make a telemedicine appointment?
faqs.a: The essential technology requirements for a telemedicine appointment are broadband internet access, audio and video capabilities, imaging technology (such as a camera), and email access. These can all be done on a phone, tablet, or computer. We will provide patients with login information to access their online portal. Patients who do not have access to these technologies may use a public computer space, such as a library, and ask for a private area during their appointment time.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover telemedicine services?
faqs.a: Most insurance providers cover telemedicine services in place of physical appointments. Coverage generally includes any services that would be covered by an in-person visit. We recommend patients contact their insurance provider prior to seeking treatment to ensure coverage and any out-of-pocket costs.

faqs.q: Are telemedicine appointments secure?
faqs.a: Telemedicine has become more secure than ever. Patient information and data are available only to patients and their various providers (physicians, specialists, etc.). Screen sharing and video conferencing use encrypted screen capture and all data is encrypted within the portal. Emails sent through telecommunications are encrypted and require patients to log in through the portal to access the information.

title: Urinary Tract Infection Aliso Viejo, CA | Orange County House Calls | Treating UTIs
description: Primary care doctors can provide patients with urinary tract infection treatment to reduce painful symptoms and prevent the infection from spreading.
h1: Urinary Tract Infection Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
A urinary tract infection (UTI) can be incredibly painful and hard to manage. It is important to seek the proper care to prevent the infection from spreading to the kidneys. While prevention is the best way to deal with urinary tract infections, they can still occur regardless of preventive measures.

With proper treatment, a primary care doctor can help patients manage UTI symptoms and treat the infection promptly. Urinary tract infection treatment is available at Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area. Call us today at (949) 204-1334 to schedule an appointment or learn more about our services.

Understanding Urinary Tract Infections

A urinary tract infection, also known as a bladder infection, is an infection that occurs anywhere in the urinary system, including the kidneys, bladder, and urethra. UTIs commonly occur in the lower urinary tract, where the bladder and urethra are located. While minor UTIs are often treatable at home with antibiotics and proper cleansing, severe UTIs can result in a kidney infection. People experiencing persistent or painful symptoms should seek professional care to relieve symptoms faster and ensure proper treatment.

There are various causes for a urinary tract infection. It occurs due to bacteria or fungi that enter the urinary tract and multiply rapidly. Anything that can irritate the urinary tract can lead to an infection. Also, sexual activity and the presence of a sexually transmitted disease puts patients at an increased risk. Urinary tract infections occur mainly in women, especially while pregnant.

A urinary tract infection, also known as a bladder infection, is an infection that occurs anywhere in the urinary system, including the kidneys, bladder, and urethra.

Symptoms of a Urinary Tract Infection

Symptoms of lower UTIs are typically far less severe than ones that occur in the upper tract. Other factors that can impact symptom severity include the gender of the individual and the cause of the infection. A urinary infection that takes place in the lower tract affects the urethra and the bladder. The most common symptoms include:

  • Burning while urinating
  • Cloudy, pink, or even bloody urine
  • Increased sensation to urinate
  • Mild to severe pain
  • Strong odor in urine

In most cases, a lower urinary tract infection can be treated with medical assistance and does not take long to recover. An upper UTI, which affects the kidneys, typically has a longer recovery period and can be life-threatening if not properly dealt with. The most common symptoms of an upper urinary tract infection include pain in and around the urinary tract, fever and chills, nausea, and vomiting. While UTI symptoms are about the same in men and women, there are some slight differences.

For example, UTI infections in men can cause pain in the rectal region, while women often feel pain in the pelvic region. Pain can also be present in the back, where the kidneys are located. Seeing a primary care doctor for a UTI can minimize discomfort and help prevent the infection from worsening.

The most common symptoms of an upper urinary tract infection include pain in and around the urinary tract, fever and chills, nausea, and vomiting.

Urinary Tract Infection Diagnosis and Treatment

A primary care doctor can provide people that are experiencing UTI symptoms with an accurate diagnosis and prompt treatment. Diagnosis often includes analyzing a urine sample and documenting the patient's symptoms. In some cases, a laboratory test may be necessary to determine the exact type of bacteria causing the infection. This type of test ultimately helps us provide the proper treatment for recovery. In some instances, imaging of the urinary tract is also helpful for diagnosis.

Antibiotics can treat UTIs caused by bacteria. Lower tract infections usually only require oral antibiotics, while an upper tract infection may require intravenous antibiotics. For bacterial urinary tract infections, antibiotics are usually the only form of treatment that can help relieve the symptoms. In some cases, our primary care doctor can prescribe a painkiller to minimize discomfort.

Lower tract infections usually only require oral antibiotics, while an upper tract infection may require intravenous antibiotics.

The Recovery Process

The earlier people receive treatment for a urinary tract infection, the better. Without treatment, UTI symptoms can worsen, especially if the infection occurs in the upper tract. While treatment is important, people can also take certain actions to help keep the symptoms tolerable and help the recovery process.

Drinking plenty of water with a urinary tract infection can significantly reduce pain and symptoms. It may seem counterproductive as urination becomes more frequent and can be painful, but it is important for recovery. Also, the process of urinating helps with the infection. Resisting the urge to urinate can aggravate the infection and make it worse.

Drinking plenty of water with a urinary tract infection can significantly reduce pain and symptoms.

When To Seek Treatment for a UTI

It is important to visit a primary care doctor for UTI treatment during its early stages to ensure proper treatment and recovery. It is crucial to seek treatment from a primary care doctor since misdiagnosing the cause of the urinary tract infection can lead to the wrong treatment. People who experience chronic UTIs that last for an extended amount of time despite treatment may be referred to a specialist to determine the right diagnosis and treatment.

Pregnant women experiencing a urinary tract infection should receive treatment right away since it can increase the chance of the infection spreading to the kidneys. This can cause high blood pressure or premature delivery. If symptoms begin to worsen and become severe, seek medical assistance right away. Severe symptoms may mean that the infection is in the kidneys, which can be life-threatening if left untreated for too long.

It is important to visit a primary care doctor for UTI treatment during its early stages to ensure proper treatment and recovery.

Call Us Today

Seeing a primary care doctor for UTI treatment can ensure a quick and full recovery. Our team at Orange County House Calls can help. Call us today at 949-204-1334 to learn more about our services to schedule an appointment or learn more about our services.

faqs.q: If left untreated, can a urinary tract infection spread to other parts of the body?
faqs.a: Yes, a urinary tract infection can spread to other parts of the urinary tract and the body. In fact, the fear of the infection spreading is why it is such a serious matter, especially upper tract infections. The biggest concern of an infection left untreated is that it will reach the kidneys. If a urinary tract infection reaches the kidneys, then the condition may be considered life-threatening.

faqs.q: What factors put individuals at an increased risk of developing a urinary tract infection?
faqs.a: Women are far more at risk of developing a urinary tract infection than men, especially while pregnant. The existence of a sexually transmitted disease can place you at an increased risk as well. Additionally, anything that irritates the urinary system could lead to an infection, such as holding in urine, not drinking enough water, or not receiving the proper dosage of vitamins. Also, the risk of developing urinary tract infections increases with age.

faqs.q: I know urinary tract infections are fairly common in women but are they common in men as well?
faqs.a: Women have a much higher risk of developing a urinary tract infection than men. However, urinary tract infections are very common, so men should also take precautions. In most cases, the symptoms in both men and women are almost the same.

faqs.q: Does drinking more water provide relief from a urinary tract infection?
faqs.a: Drinking more water may not provide relief to the symptoms of a urinary tract infection — which typically include pain while urinating and discoloration of the urine — but it often helps the recovery process. While suffering from a urinary tract infection, the first reaction is often not to drink water as it causes urination, which can be painful. However, drinking water and urinating often are both important factors in recovering from a urinary tract infection.

faqs.q: Peeing is very painful when I have a urinary tract infection. Should I try and limit the amount I pee to avoid complicating the urinary tract infection?
faqs.a: In most cases, there is likely not to be much that comes out when urinating with a UTI. However, it is important to try anyway. Doing so can help the urinary system flush out the infection and fully recover.

title: Vomiting and Diarrhea Treatment Aliso Viejo, CA | Orange County House Calls | Treating Nausea & Vomiting
description: People suffering from vomiting or diarrhea can receive medical treatment from a primary care doctor who can address the root cause of the issue.
h1: Vomiting and Diarrhea Treatment Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
Vomiting and diarrhea can be extremely unpleasant and cause a significant amount of discomfort. In most cases, these symptoms are not indicative of a severe health concern. However, it is crucial to seek professional medical treatment if they persist for several days or more. Our primary care doctor can help to determine the most effective course of symptom relief.

Even though people are quick to dismiss vomiting and diarrhea cases as minor, the discomfort can worsen over time. Our team at Orange County House Calls are here to help. Call us at (949) 204-1334 to learn more about our services or schedule an appointment.

Seeing a Primary Care Doctor for Vomiting and Diarrhea

Vomiting is the forceful expulsion of the stomach's contents through the mouth, while diarrhea is loose and watery stools that occur at least three times a day. While preventing the onset of vomiting and diarrhea is ideal, it is not always possible since it is often unpredictable. Vomiting and diarrhea may be a sign of a health condition that requires medical care. Excessive vomiting can lead to dehydration which can result in other health complications.

People experiencing vomiting or diarrhea that persists for more than a couple of days should see a primary care doctor. We can conduct an examination and determine the most effective treatment plan to help manage symptoms.

We can conduct an examination and determine the most effective treatment plan to help manage symptoms.

Causes of Vomiting and Diarrhea

If the patient cannot determine the exact cause of the vomiting or diarrhea, we will help them go over anything they have consumed in the past few hours or days. In cases where the cause is unknown, we will run an examination to determine a diagnosis and provide the patient with the treatment they need. While there are numerous reasons why a person may exhibit the symptoms, here are several of the more common causes of vomiting and diarrhea:

  • Consumption of spoiled food
  • Overconsumption of food or alcohol
  • Stress
  • Pregnancy
  • Stomach viruses

The primary causes of vomiting and diarrhea include food poisoning and stomach viruses. Another common cause of vomiting and diarrhea is overconsumption, whether it be food, alcohol, or some form of medication. While overeating food generally does not pose much of a health risk, consuming too much alcohol or drugs can have serious long-term health risks. It is essential to seek medical attention if this is a probable cause of the symptoms. Also, it is not uncommon for too much stress to cause vomiting and, in some cases, diarrhea. Lastly, if there is a chance of being pregnant, the patient must take vomiting and nausea seriously.

The primary causes of vomiting and diarrhea include food poisoning and stomach viruses.

Vomiting and Diarrhea Treatment Options

Knowing the underlying cause of vomiting and diarrhea is essential for determining the right treatment. In some instances, a bacteria or virus can release a substance or toxin that can cause vomiting or diarrhea. When the body comes across an unfamiliar or harmful substance, it tries to remove the substance as quickly as possible. While this is helpful for the body, too much vomiting or diarrhea can lead to dehydration and other serious health concerns.

Symptoms that last for an extended period or cause severe complications will require professional medical intervention. When experiencing excessive vomiting or diarrhea, it is crucial to remain hydrated. A primary care doctor can provide people with an oral rehydration solution (ORS) to replace lost fluids and nutrients. People should also avoid taking any medications unless authorized to do so by a medical professional. If patients rely on specific medications that they cannot keep down, they should let our team know. In some cases, pumping the stomach may be necessary if a patient has consumed something lethal to their health.

…a bacteria or virus can release a substance or toxin that can cause vomiting or diarrhea.

How to Prevent Vomiting and Diarrhea

It can be difficult to prevent vomiting and diarrhea as various conditions can cause them to occur. However, there are some actions that people can take to help prevent vomiting and diarrhea from occurring in the first place. Some precautions may include:

  • Avoiding undercooked or raw foods
  • Being cautious around individuals who are sick
  • Practicing proper hygiene
  • Staying home and resting when sick

Practicing good hygiene includes washing hands often with soap and water, cleaning frequently used surfaces around the home, and not touching the eyes and mouth, especially after sneezing or touching a doorknob. Additionally, staying at home and resting while sick with the cold or flu can help the body fight off infection. While it is not always possible to prevent vomiting or diarrhea, seeing a primary care doctor can ensure that people receive the prompt treatment they need to manage their symptoms.

It can be difficult to prevent vomiting and diarrhea as various conditions can cause them to occur.

Call Us Today

A primary care doctor can effectively and safely diagnose and treat vomiting and diarrhea symptoms. Our team at Orange County House Calls can determine the right treatment plan to alleviate your symptoms and prevent dehydration. Call us today at 949-204-1334 to learn more about our services or schedule an appointment.

faqs.q: Is it okay not to eat or drink while I am suffering from vomiting and diarrhea?
faqs.a: It is important to continue eating and drinking while suffering from vomiting and diarrhea to prevent dehydration. With that said, there are certain foods and drinks you should avoid, including anything that makes you nauseous. Instead, try eating thin soup and taking small sips of water throughout the day.

faqs.q: I believe I ate something bad, which has caused me to have vomiting and diarrhea. How long should I wait before visiting a primary care doctor?
faqs.a: In general, vomiting and diarrhea for any cause, especially for food poisoning, should not last more than 72 hours. However, if the symptoms become extremely concerning at any point within the first three days, the individual should seek prompt medical care. While an adequately treated case of vomiting and diarrhea is not extremely concerning, dehydration can cause severe health concerns.

faqs.q: What are the warning signs of dehydration?
faqs.a: Symptoms of dehydration often include extreme thirst and dark yellow urine. Additionally, people may experience muscle cramps and a headache before dehydration begins to set in. More concerning symptoms of dehydration include dizziness, fatigue, and a rapid heartbeat.

faqs.q: I need to take my medication, but I keep throwing it back up. What do I need to do?
faqs.a: People with a condition that requires them to take medicine daily can experience great difficulty if the vomiting prevents them from keeping their medication down. If this is happening to you, you are not alone. Patients should speak to their primary care doctor for further instruction or advice on managing this issue.

h1: Weight Loss Treatment Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
Weight loss programs have gained extreme popularity over the past few decades, but many of them are detrimental to our health and well-being. Choosing a weight loss program through a qualified physician or specialist provides more realistic and achievable outcomes while keeping health in mind. We can curate an individualized treatment plan that works best for your goals, lifestyle habits, and current health status.

Weight loss treatments are available at Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area for patients looking to improve both their health and appearance. Our team works to help you attain the body you want in a healthy way. To learn more about a procedure or schedule an appointment, call (949) 204-1334 today.

Medical Weight Loss

Medical weight loss at Orange County HouseCalls offers a personalized, physician-guided approach to achieving and maintaining a healthy weight. Unlike one-size-fits-all programs or fad diets, our medical weight loss plans are tailored to each patient’s unique health profile, lifestyle, and goals. Under the supervision of a board-certified Internal Medicine physician, we take the time to evaluate underlying factors that may be contributing to weight gain, including metabolic conditions, hormonal imbalances, medications, and lifestyle habits.

Our program focuses on safe, sustainable results through a combination of clinical evaluation, individualized nutrition guidance, lifestyle modifications, and, when appropriate, evidence-based medical therapies. Patients receive ongoing support, regular follow-up, and adjustments to their plan to ensure steady progress and long-term success. This comprehensive approach not only helps with weight reduction but also improves overall health, including blood pressure, blood sugar control, energy levels, and cardiovascular risk.

Designed for busy individuals who value convenience and personalized care, our medical weight loss services can be delivered through in-home visits or telemedicine, allowing you to receive expert guidance without disrupting your daily routine. Whether your goal is to lose weight, improve your health, or prevent chronic disease, our program provides a structured, medically supervised path to help you achieve lasting results in a safe and supportive environment.

What is Overweight and Obesity?

Most patients looking into weight loss programs fall under the overweight or obese categories. We look at the Body Mass Index (BMI) to determine where a patient fits in regards to their weight. BMI refers to the measure of a person's weight in relation to their height. Overweight individuals fall between 25 to 30 on the BMI scale while obese individuals have a BMI over 30.

According to the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, "Obesity is a chronic disease that affects more than 4 in 10 adults in the United States, and nearly 1 in 10 Americans have severe obesity." Although obesity is a chronic condition, a healthy lifestyle and diet changes can tremendously impact weight loss. A healthy lifestyle and diet encompass regular physical exercise, a meal plan, and routine physical checkups and exams.

Overweight individuals fall between 25 to 30 on the BMI scale while obese individuals have a BMI over 30.

How Weight Affects Health

Excess weight, or chronic weight, has many detrimental effects on overall health. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that individuals who are obese are at an increased risk of acquiring various diseases and serious health conditions, such as:

  • All causes of death (mortality)
  • Body pain and difficulty with physical functioning
  • Coronary heart disease
  • Gallbladder disease
  • High blood pressure (Hypertension)
  • High LDL cholesterol, low HDL cholesterol, or high levels of triglycerides (Dyslipidemia)
  • Low quality of life
  • Many types of cancer
  • Mental illness such as clinical depression, anxiety, and other mental disorders
  • Osteoarthritis (a breakdown of cartilage and bone within a joint)
  • Sleep apnea and breathing problems
  • Type 2 diabetes

The body functions as a machine. Each body part and organ in our body systems work together, each one linked to the next one in line. When one part is not functioning as intended, other parts start to wear or break down. One aspect of the body, weight, is connected to all of the other parts of the body. A healthy weight sets the stage for bones, muscles, brain, heart, and others to do their jobs effectively and efficiently.

Each body part and organ in our body systems work together, each one linked to the next one in line.

Understanding Weight Loss Treatment

Weight loss programs involve the use of one or more treatments or medications that help improve cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of complications related to obesity. A medical professional who treats chronic weight and obesity problems can curate a personalized treatment plan. They take into account the patient's medical history, medications they are currently taking, and any allergies or sensitivities they may have.

Weight loss prescription medications work by making an individual feel less hungry, full sooner, or making it harder for the body to absorb fats from the foods a person consumes. Each medication works differently, but they each target a problem the patient has. FDA-approved weight loss medications include Bupropion-naltrexone (Contrave), Liraglutide (Saxenda), Orlistat (Xenical), and Phentermine-topiramate (Qsymia). The FDA recently approved a weight loss injection medication called Wegovy (semaglutide) for patients who are obese or overweight and have at least one chronic condition due to their weight. Alongside medication, patients' treatment plans may consist of a meal plan, foods and beverages list, exercise plan, and any other changes pertaining to their lifestyle and condition.

Weight loss programs involve the use of one or more treatments and/or medications that help improve cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of complications related to obesity.

Healthy vs Unhealthy Weight Loss

Trendy non-medical weight loss programs tend to have one goal in mind: losing weight. That could be the primary goal of a client as well. However, most diets and fads induce temporary weight loss while affecting other parts of the body. It is important to know and understand the difference between healthy and unhealthy weight loss.

Unhealthy weight loss programs may help patients lose weight faster, but the weight loss usually only lasts for a brief time. Healthy weight loss (about one to two pounds per week) has been shown to keep the weight off longer and keep individuals motivated to continue eating a healthy diet and exercising. The CDC explains, "Even a modest weight loss of five to 10 percent of your total body weight is likely to produce health benefits, such as improvements in blood pressure, blood cholesterol, and blood sugar." Treatment plans for long-term weight loss should consist of a combination of medication, physical activity, and a healthy diet.

Unhealthy weight loss may help patients lose weight faster, but it usually only lasts for a brief time.

Types of Treatments Available

After discussing the patient's goals, past, current, and future health status, health risks, and types of treatments, we will create a treatment plan together. This involves patients in their own treatment and allows them to take charge of their life and health. Although every treatment plan differs, typical treatment plans include lifestyle changes, exercise and physical activity, behavioral changes, medications, and procedures or surgeries.

Lifestyle changes may consist of cutting calories, eating foods with healthier sugars (fruits and vegetables), eating more proteins, restricting certain foods, and replacing snacks and meals. They will always involve exercise and physical activity in any way the patient likes. Behavior changes help many patients lose weight; this can include modifying behavior through counseling or support groups. Some treatment plans include medications, as stated before.

Lastly, in severe cases, we may require or recommend a procedure or surgery. Endoscopic procedures include sleeve gastroplasty and intragastric balloon. Both procedures reduce space in the stomach to prevent overeating. Weight loss surgeries include adjustable gastric banding, gastric bypass surgery, and gastric sleeve. Patients who undergo a procedure or surgery must still commit to lifelong changes in their eating and exercise habits to ensure treatment success.

Although every treatment plan differs, typical treatment plans include lifestyle changes, exercise and physical activity, behavioral changes, medications, and procedures or surgeries.

Weight loss consultations and treatments are available at our office. The Orange County House Calls team looks forward to treating you, helping you lose weight healthily, and preventing health conditions from arising or progressing. Call our office at 949-204-1334 to learn more or schedule an appointment.

faqs.q: What is medical weight loss treatment?
faqs.a: Medical weight loss treatment refers to weight loss programs managed and overseen by a medical professional. They curate a custom treatment plan for each individual based on their current health status and medical history, including any conditions they have and medications they are taking. A medical weight loss treatment may consist of medications, lifestyle and behavioral modifications, procedures, or surgeries.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of taking prescription weight loss medications?
faqs.a: Prescription medications are not for everyone. However, people who take prescription medications as part of a lifestyle program lose three to 12% more of their starting body weight than people in a lifestyle program who do not take medication. Weight loss medications also help improve health by lowering blood sugar, blood pressure, and triglyceride levels and reducing problems related to overweight and obesity, such as joint pain and sleep apnea.

faqs.q: What risks do weight loss medications hold?
faqs.a: Risks and side effects vary by medication and how a person's body reacts. In most cases, however, side effects are minor and subside after the body becomes used to the new drug. Side effects of weight-loss medications include nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, constipation, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, dry mouth, diarrhea, increased blood pressure, and fast heartbeat, among others.

faqs.q: How long will I need to take my weight loss medication?
faqs.a: The amount of time weight loss medications must be taken depends on whether the medication worked (over 12 weeks) and whether the patient had any serious side effects. In most cases, medications that help patients lose weight (at least five percent of your starting weight after 12 weeks) will be recommended indefinitely, along with lifestyle and diet changes. However, patients taking medications that do not help in losing weight or produce side effects may be advised to stop immediately. We alter treatment plans throughout a patient's weight loss journey and can make any recommendations as needed, which may include a referral to a bariatric surgeon for surgery.

faqs.q: If obesity is a chronic condition, is it always genetic?
faqs.a: In many cases of obesity, genetics are the primary factor. Chronic energy imbalance results in excess weight in a person who consistently takes in more calories from food. However, not all chronic conditions, including obesity, are genetic. Some conditions arise during the span of our lifetime and stay with us for the rest of our lives. Chronic conditions must be continually monitored and managed and do not go away on their own.

html:
Seeing a primary care doctor is an important component of overall wellness and health. A primary care doctor can provide preventative wellness exams to help patients maintain their overall health. Do not hesitate to see your primary care doctor; early detection and treatment are key for positive outcomes.

Wellness exams are available at Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area. Our team is here to help you improve and maintain your quality of life. Call us today at (949) 204-1334 to learn more about our services or schedule an appointment.

Understanding Wellness Visits

  • Birth Control

Regular wellness visits with a primary care doctor are an important way to ensure good health and wellness. While many people believe that they can skip these visits if they are healthy, this is not true. A wellness visit is a form of preventative care. Preventative care focuses on maintaining wellness and preventing health issues from developing or worsening.

Rather than waiting until a health problem occurs, a patient can visit their doctor while they are in good health to catch health issues in their early stages. These visits usually occur yearly and are separate from other medical visits. They provide patients and primary care doctors with a status update on overall health, both mental and physical. This information can help both parties promote better health and wellness and make healthier choices.

Regular wellness visits with a primary care doctor are an important way to ensure good health and wellness.

Wellness Services

Keeping up with regular wellness and health exams is one of the key components of treating illnesses and other health issues. When conducting wellness visits, we take various factors about a patient's health into account, including:

  • Age
  • Current condition
  • Diet and lifestyle
  • Exercise
  • Medical history
  • Medications

A wellness visit can help primary care doctors identify the source of a patient's health issue and address it properly. Possible aspects of a wellness visit may include checking vitals, screenings, discussions about current lifestyle choices, and establishing a health plan. Our team may also ask patients about their current stress, physical activity, diet, and drug or alcohol usage. A wellness exam aims to improve overall health through lifestyle and health decision-making.

Possible aspects of a wellness visit may include checking vitals, screenings, discussions about current lifestyle choices, and establishing a health plan.

The Importance of Preventative Care

Preventative care can help patients prepare and protect themselves from various general illnesses or conditions. Seeking treatment during the early stages of a general illness can produce better treatment outcomes. During a wellness visit, we can detect issues that may become more serious problems in the future.

Preventative care is important for patients 18 years of age and older. Even if a patient does not have a specific health issue, a wellness visit can provide them with valuable information about their health status. We recommend patients receive a wellness check once a year.

Seeking treatment during the early stages of a general illness can produce better treatment outcomes.

Preparing for a Wellness Visit

During a wellness visit, patients should be prepared to discuss their health and an illness prevention plan. While an annual wellness exam does not usually include a physical exam, it typically includes taking the patient's height, weight, and blood pressure measurements. A primary care doctor may also review a patient's medications and discuss their health risk assessment.

Before a wellness visit, patients should write down any questions that they have for their doctor. It is also helpful to bring a list of any medications currently taken. Patients should also expect to share their health concerns and family health history so the primary care doctor can perform the right health screenings. After the visit, our team may recommend certain tests, referrals to specialists, or follow-up appointments to ensure patient wellness.

Patients should also expect to share their health concerns and family health history so the primary care doctor can perform the right health screenings.

faqs.q: What are vital signs?
faqs.a: Vital signs include the four to six most important medical signs that help indicate the status of the body's vital functions. These measurements can also indicate possible disease and show progression towards recovery. The main vital signs include pulse rate, temperature, respiration rate, and blood pressure.

faqs.q: What are some possible health screenings that I can receive?
faqs.a: A health screening is a medical test that doctors use to check patients for diseases and other health conditions before they experience signs or symptoms. Finding problems early on allows them to be much more treatable. The type of screening depends on a person's age, sex, and medical history. Possible health screenings include ones for certain types of cancers, high blood pressure, sexually transmitted diseases, and diabetes.

faqs.q: How is blood pressure measured?
faqs.a: Regularly measuring blood pressure allows primary care doctors to diagnose health issues early. If a patient's blood pressure is too high, our team can work with them to take the necessary steps to control their levels. Digital blood pressure monitors placed on a patient's finder or upper arm can read a patient's blood pressure based on variations in blood volume in the arteries.

faqs.q: Why is it important for a primary care doctor to know about all the medications a patient is taking?
faqs.a: Patients should notify any medical professional about all the medications they are taking. Without this information, medication reconciliation problems are possible. Adverse drug events accounted for about 700,000 emergency room visits as of 2015. Providing this relevant information will allow a primary care doctor to make safe and effective prescriptions for patients.

faqs.q: How can stress affect my wellness?
faqs.a: The symptoms of stress can affect a patient's health even if they do not realize it. Stress can adversely affect a patient's body, thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. These can lead to headaches, insomnia, decreased work productivity, and more. Leaving stress unchecked can contribute to various health problems, from high blood pressure to diabetes.

description: Falls happen to millions of older adults each year. A primary care doctor can provide personalized treatment and prevention education to keep loved ones safe.
h1: When An Older Person Falls Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
Falls can happen to anyone. However, falls are especially common occurrences in older people, 65 years and older. While falls can be a serious problem for older people, the right education and prevention techniques can help protect your loved one.

When a fall happens, a primary care provider can give your loved ones with the personalized attention they deserve. Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area can help. Call us at (949) 204-1334 to learn more about our services.

Falls Are a Common Problem

As people get older, their muscles weaken, their balance decreases, and they become more likely to fall. One-quarter of Americans will be older than 65 years by the year 2030. According to the CDC, falls are a common problem among this population, with about 36 million older adults falling each year.

While it is easy for younger people to stay upright, aging can bring about factors that challenge balance and strength. Medications, vision impairments, and general weakness combined with environmental factors can put older people at risk of falling. While falls are a common problem in older adults, raising awareness and using the right prevention techniques can prevent them from happening.

According to the CDC, falls are a common problem among this population, with about 36 million older adults falling each year.

Gauging the Extent of the Problem

When a fall occurs in an older person, it is important to gauge the extent of harm that the fall caused. Looking for signs of lacerations, skin tears, bruising, and joint deformities can help determine the fall severity. It is also crucial to look for any signs of a moderate to serious head injury.

Signs and symptoms to be aware of include abnormal behavior, excessive sleepiness, severe headaches, stiff neck, unequal pupil sizes, fainting, and vomiting. Some head injury symptoms can take a while to appear. Therefore, it is important to keep a lookout for any signs that could indicate a serious injury in the hours and days after the fall.

Looking for signs of lacerations, skin tears, bruising, and joint deformities can help determine the fall severity.

Signs That a Fall Occurred

While more than one out of four older adults fall each year, only half will tell their doctor. If there is suspicion that a fall has occurred, it is crucial to ask the right questions and look for signs. Older people may be reluctant to speak about the fall due to embarrassment or a fear of losing their independence. They may try to downplay these incidents to prevent them from having to rely on others. However, this prevents them from receiving the proper support and prevention measures.

When a fall is suspected, ask them if they are experiencing any pain, the pain location, and how severe it is. Sometimes family members can be non-responsive or have communicative issues that prevent them from explaining what happened. It is important to recognize symptoms such as confusion, dizziness, numbness, or difficulty breathing in these cases. Through communication and observation, try to pinpoint where an injury may have occurred and if there is any bleeding, bruising, or other signs of injury.

While more than one out of four older people fall each year, only half will tell their doctor.

How a Primary Care Doctor Can Help

When an older person has fallen, a primary care doctor can provide timely and reliable access to the care they need. Information about the fall's height, the surface on which the patient fell, and the point of impact will help us anticipate injury patterns and determine the patient's risk for severe injury. Elderly patients can have significant injuries despite minor symptoms.

We will go over their medical history and perform a thorough physical examination to look for common injuries such as lacerations, sprains, and fractures during the physical examination and determine the best treatment course. We will distinguish which patients can have treatment in a primary care office setting and which patients will require transfer to a higher level of care. Even if the patient only has minor injuries, we will take the time to provide proper education to prevent falls in the future.

When an older person has fallen, a primary care doctor can provide timely and easy access to the care they need.

Preventing Falls in the Home

The best way to prevent falls is to address and minimize risks before they can threaten an aging loved one's health. Taking certain precautions can extend a senior's independence and help them feel more confident in their own homes. Older people can make small but effective modifications to their homes to prevent falls from happening. Helpful modifications include:

  • Altering prescription medications
  • Installing grab bars
  • Physical or occupational therapy
  • Reducing clutter
  • Using a medical alert system
  • Using a mobility aid
The best way to prevent falls is to address and minimize risks before they can threaten an aging loved one’s health.

Call Us Today

If your loved one has fallen, our primary care team can help assess their injuries and provide personalized treatment and prevention education. Orange County House Calls offers quality primary care to Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area. To learn more about our services, call us at 949-204-1334 today.

faqs.q: What can happen after a fall?
faqs.a: Many falls do not cause injuries. However, one out of five falls results in a serious injury such as a broken bone or a head injury. These injuries can make it difficult for a person to go about their everyday activities or live independently.

faqs.q: What should I do if I witness someone fall, but they do not seem seriously injured?
faqs.a: If you witness someone fall, do not try to get the person up immediately. First, check for any serious signs of injury such as serious bleeding, bruising, or swelling. If there are no obvious signs of injury and do not seem badly hurt, assist them in a comfortable position. Help them get medical help to ensure that there are no problems or injuries.

faqs.q: What are the behavioral risk factors of falling?
faqs.a: There are behavioral risk factors that people may or may not realize they are doing that contribute to their risk of falling. Risk factors include limited physical activity and exercise and poor nutrition and fluid intake, increasing weakness and stability. Wearing inappropriate clothing, footwear, or engaging in risky behaviors like carrying, reaching, and bending can also increase the risk of falling.

faqs.q: Why are older people more prone to falling?
faqs.a: Many factors can cause older people to fall more easily. However, the three main reasons include chronic health conditions, impairments, and balance affecting illnesses. There are many chronic health conditions, but heart disease, dementia, or low blood pressure can cause dizziness. Impairments can include anything from lines of poor vision or muscle weakness. Any illness that affects balance can increase the risk of falling.

faqs.q: Is there a common time of day when falls occur the most often?
faqs.a: Most falls occur at particular times of the day. Many falls occur early in the morning when people are drowsy after waking up or late at night when they are tired and heading upstairs to bed. It is especially important to go slow, be careful, and take frequent pauses to avoid falling during these times.

title: When to Seek Care for Ear Pain Aliso Viejo, CA | Orange County House Calls | Treating Earaches and Ear Pain
description: People with ear pain that persists longer than a few days and accompanies other adverse symptoms should seek care from a primary care doctor.
h1: When to Seek Care for Ear Pain Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
People with severe ear pain that does not go away within a few days or accompanies other symptoms such as a fever or sore throat should seek care. Ear pain alone is generally not concerning and will usually go away by itself after a few days. However, ear pain with other symptoms may signify a more severe condition that requires medical attention.

The causes of ear pain can range from minor issues to severe health issues. Our team at Orange County House Calls in Aliso Viejo and the surrounding area provides care for ear pain. Call us today at (949) 204-1334 to schedule an appointment with our primary care doctor or learn more about our services.

Understanding Ear Pain

While ear pain is not as common in adults, some may struggle with it. People do not have to experience an infection or something wrong with their ears to experience ear pain. There are many different possible causes of ear pain, including a middle ear infection, outer ear infection, air pressure changes, or earwax buildup.

Ear pain may also accompany trauma to the head. In this case, people should seek prompt medical attention as it may indicate a brain injury. While it is possible to manage ear pain at home, in some cases, people must see a primary care doctor for professional medical care.

People do not have to have an infection or something wrong with their ears to experience ear pain.

Ear Pain Symptoms

The symptoms of ear pain will vary depending on its underlying cause. For example, a middle ear infection causes fluid to build up inside the inner ear and Eustachian tube. This may lead to symptoms such as ear pain, fever, and difficulty sleeping. While not all symptoms are indicative of an issue that requires professional medical intervention, some are.

People with a fever of 102.2°F or higher or experiencing hearing loss should see a primary care doctor for treatment before any damage becomes permanent. Pain that does not start to subside until about 24 to 48 hours after also requires medical attention. A low fever or discharge from the ear may be a sign of infection, while pain that worsens when blowing the nose or tugging on the earlobe may indicate a more severe issue.

While people may want to wait out their ear pain at home, a professional examination and treatment are crucial. Even if the symptoms do not seem severe, they can become more severe over time. Our team can help to diagnose the source of the pain and recommend treatment.

The symptoms of ear pain will vary depending on its underlying cause.

Treatment for Ear Pain

A primary care doctor may prescribe antibiotics for ear pain caused by an infection. These antibiotics will usually come in the form of ear drops. It is essential to complete the entire course of antibiotics for an ear infection, even after the ear pain has disappeared. Otherwise, the bacteria that initially triggered the infection may cause the ear infection to return.

Over-the-counter decongestants may be given to patients with ear pain resulting from congestion. A primary care doctor can recommend the right dose for a child's specific needs by taking their pain levels, age, and other bodily factors into account.

A primary care doctor may prescribe antibiotics for ear pain caused by an infection.

Ear Pain Caused By Other Illnesses

Ear pain can be symptomatic of many illnesses other than ear infections. For example, inner ear pain is often a sign of mastoiditis, auditory tube disruption, or a ruptured eardrum. Mastoiditis is a rare condition in which a middle ear infection has spread to the mastoid bone, causing headaches and redness or swelling behind the ear.

Auditory tube dysfunction can also cause ear pain when the auditory tube opens or closes abnormally. This condition frequently occurs due to sudden atmospheric pressure changes, such as when one goes scuba diving. Auditory tube disruption may also lead to ruptured eardrums. Other illnesses that can lead to referred ear pain, which is ear pain that indicates a problem elsewhere in the body.

The ears are connected to other parts of the neck and head, especially the nose and throat. Some common examples of referred ear pain include sinusitis, temporomandibular joint disorder (TMJ/TMD), and tonsillitis. Our team can determine the cause of a patient's ear pain to determine the optimal treatment plan for their needs.

Ear pain can be symptomatic of many illnesses other than ear infections.

Call Us Today

When experiencing persistent ear pain, seeking professional care from a primary care doctor is crucial to minimize discomfort and prevent further complications. Our team at Orange County House Calls is here to help. Call us today at 949-204-1334 to learn more about our services or schedule an appointment.

faqs.q: What causes ear pain?
faqs.a: The most common cause of pain in the ear is an infection. It is essential to seek medical attention if the pain is not getting better. Other causes of ear pain include excessive ear wax, a change in air pressure, or another problem near the ear.

faqs.q: Can a loud noise cause ear pain?
faqs.a: People who have jobs that regularly expose them to loud sounds, such as industrial equipment, may be at risk for acoustic trauma. Acoustic trauma causes damage to the eardrum and the muscles in the inner ear. Symptoms may include a buzzing sound, ear pain, and hearing loss.

faqs.q: How is an ear infection treated?
faqs.a: A primary care doctor can diagnose an ear infection by examining the inner ear. If the ear infection is not improving, a doctor may prescribe antibiotics for a bacterial infection. For minor infections, ear drops can help reduce the pain. In extreme cases, surgery may be required if the pain does not go away.

faqs.q: What is acute otitis media?
faqs.a: Acute otitis media (AOM) is a type of ear infection in one or both ears. It is the most common type of ear infection. It is a short-term infection that comes on suddenly, causing sharp pain in the ear. This infection can occur after swelling in the middle ear, leading to eardrum pressure and pain.

faqs.q: Is swimmer's ear contagious?
faqs.a: Swimmer's ear happens when water is trapped in the ear canal and allows bacteria to grow. Individuals may notice pain when pulling on the earlobe. However, because the bacteria are inside the ear, this infection is not contagious. We may recommend antibiotic ear drops to help treat the symptoms.

title: When to Seek Treatment for Neck Pain Aliso Viejo, CA | Orange County House Calls | Treating Neck Pain
description: If you have a stiff or painful neck that interferes with your everyday activities, a primary care physician may be able to help. Do not hesitate.
h1: When to Seek Treatment for Neck Pain Aliso Viejo, CA
html:
Neck pain can make it difficult to enjoy life. You do your best to participate in the things you love, but when your neck is stiff or hurts, it can be hard to do anything. Many individuals suffering from neck pain may even choose not to get out of bed.

If your neck pain keeps you from getting the most out of life, it is time to visit a doctor. Once you receive an official diagnosis, you can finally begin a treatment plan and get one step closer to alleviating that debilitating pain. If you live in or around Aliso Viejo, you can be seen at Orange County House Calls today. Call us at (949) 204-1334 to learn more about our services.

Signs That It Is Time to Go to the Doctor for Neck Pain

Sometimes, neck pain responds to self-care that includes heat, ice, and rest. Other times, however, medical attention may be necessary. Knowing which warning signs to keep in mind can help. Anyone dealing with the following symptoms should contact their primary care physician:

  • Body aches associated with flu-like symptoms
  • Lingering neck pain
  • Muscle spasms in the neck
  • Pain after a neck injury
  • Pain radiating from the neck to the shoulders, causing numbness or weakness
  • Worsening neck pain

Body Aches Associated with Flu-Like Symptoms

It is not uncommon to experience general body aches when dealing with the flu. These aches often include neck pain. A doctor can prescribe medications to reduce the severity of flu symptoms and shorten the length of time the illness will last. Those with neck pain and mild to moderate flu symptoms should immediately visit the doctor, especially if such symptoms are accompanied by fever, vomiting, headaches, and sensitivity to bright lights. Altogether, these are often signs of meningitis.

Lingering Neck Pain

Ice and heat can relieve neck pain in many cases. However, sometimes, the symptoms persist or get worse, even with the appropriate self-care. When the pain worsens or does not go away within three weeks, it could be due to an underlying medical issue. The patient may also be aggravating the muscles and tendons without realizing it. A doctor can determine the source of the pain and help manage the symptoms.

Muscle Spasms in the Neck

Muscle spasms can make the neck feel stiff, reducing mobility. The neck muscles tighten, and hard knots might form. Many patients find relief by using ice, heat, and over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medications to alleviate the symptoms. If symptoms persist after a day or two or if the spasms prevent patients from sleeping, it is time to visit a doctor. They can determine the cause of the neck pain and provide the appropriate treatment.

Pain After Neck Injury

Patients who seriously injure their necks should seek emergency assistance. However, if the pain is mild to moderate, they can visit a primary care doctor. The pain could be due to a soft tissue injury, such as a muscle sprain or strain. After examining the patient, the doctor can provide a treatment plan to help the patient recover from the injury.

Pain Radiating from the Neck to the Shoulders

Neck pain is hard enough to handle on its own, but it is even worse when it moves to the shoulders and causes muscle numbness or weakness. This pain can be debilitating, and treatment is needed to begin the healing process. A primary care doctor can prescribe oral corticosteroids to reduce inflammation and pain while alleviating the numbness. The patient might also need to wear a soft cervical collar to keep the neck in place.

It is not uncommon to experience general body aches when dealing with the flu.

Frequent Causes and Effects of Neck Pain

Severe and prolonged pain in the neck could be a sign of a serious condition. Poor posture or osteoarthritis can cause discomfort and irritation, while accidents or injuries can also damage the neck muscles. These pains may limit the affected individual's range of motion or even make routine tasks difficult. These sensations may radiate into the person's arms, hands, legs, or feet. The source of this pain can be anything from a pinched nerve, herniated disk, arthritis, meningitis, or even cancer. Only a doctor can make an official diagnosis, making it imperative to seek medical attention as soon as possible.

Severe and prolonged pain in the neck could be a sign of a serious condition.

Treatment Options for Neck Pain

Treatment options for neck pain can range from at-home remedies to medications and surgery. Often, mild pain can be alleviated with products found in your local pharmacy like Blue-Emu®, Tiger Balm®, or Bengay®. If you are experiencing chronic neck pain, it is best to talk to consult a doctor immediately. A doctor can prescribe the right treatment plan and discuss if surgery is needed.

Pain Medication

Over-the-counter drugs are a common way to treat neck pain. The doctor may examine the patient and recommend a product such as ibuprofen, Tylenol®, or aspirin. These medications can relieve pain and hold off any inflammation. If these drugs are ineffective, the doctor may write a prescription. Once the patient has taken all the required doses, the doctor will follow up and evaluate their condition.

Heat and Ice

Rotating a heating pad and ice pack throughout the day may be the right approach to getting rid of neck pain. The doctor can recommend time intervals and how long the patient should follow this process. Heat and ice treatment can reduce swelling if the patient is diligent about following this strategy for at least a few days.

Stretching and Massaging

The physician may also suggest a few types of stretches and movements the patient can try. Slow but consistent side-to-side movement of the head and neck can stretch out the muscles and relieve tightness. Patients should not attempt any of these without the approval of the doctor. Ignoring the doctor's directions could lead to further injuries and complications. With the doctor's approval, the person may also see a licensed massage therapist to soothe the muscles.

Injections and Muscle Relaxants

Steroid injections may also be an effective tactic to battle neck pain. These shots go directly into the source of pain and can relieve the pressure of a pinched nerve. Muscle relaxants are another possibility the doctor may consider. These drugs can reduce the intensity and frequency of muscle spasms in the person's neck.

Treatment options for neck pain can range from at-home remedies to medications and surgery.

When Hospitalization is Needed for Neck Pain

Neck pain is a common symptom of many conditions. While most are minor, some may require more involved care. Many times, home remedies and a visit to your primary care doctor are enough to treat neck pain. In more dire situations, however, hospitalization may be necessary. Patients experiencing the following symptoms should call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately:

  • Breathing problems
  • Heavy bleeding
  • Incontinence
  • Paralysis
  • Severe headache
  • Swelling or deformity at the injury site
  • Unconsciousness or unresponsiveness, no matter how brief

Such symptoms can indicate more severe conditions, including but not limited to meningitis. Patients' spinal cords and brains may be compromised, particularly if these symptoms are associated with traumatic injury, muscle weakness, or high fever. Other signs of neurological issues include feeling a tingling sensation, general fatigue, brain fog, and shooting pains or numbness. This is especially true for patients who have already tested negative for potential heart problems. In any case, patients should be prepared to answer questions about what type of pain they are experiencing, any possible triggers, treatments they have already tried, and more.

Referring Out to Neck Pain Specialist

While an primary care physician can help with most cases of neck pain, some patients may benefit from a more long-term relationship with a specialist. In such instances, we may refer our patients out to a physical therapist or chiropractor. Physical therapists are one of the most popular types of neck pain specialists. They apply various treatments to reduce enough pain and stiffness to begin an active program of stretching and strengthening the neck. However, the specific methods, exercises, and duration of the treatment plan vary according to each patient's needs.

A chiropractor, also known as a doctor of chiropractic, is a specialist who primarily uses manual manipulation to treat spinal and musculoskeletal problems. These manual therapies may include spinal manipulation, mobilization, and adjunctive therapies to relieve pain and improve spinal function. Spinal manipulation is the original chiropractic adjustment, and it consists of a high-velocity, low-amplitude (HVLA) thrust. In contrast, spinal mobilization consists of a low-force, gentle technique that does not twist the body.

While a primary care physician can help with most cases of neck pain, some patients may benefit from a more long-term relationship with a specialist.

Call Us Today

Unfortunately, many patients are tempted to put off going to the doctor and try to deal with neck pain alone. While this approach may work for minor issues, individuals should seek immediate medical attention for pain that increases or does not subside with home treatment. A primary care physician can use different methods to reduce the pain and make an official diagnosis.

If you live in or near Aliso Viejo and need relief from back pain, do not delay. Walk into Orange County House Calls today. Call us today at 949-204-1334 to learn more about our services.
